title: Head arrangements versus written parts; teacher Walter LaVernie and breathing
summary: He prefers playing by head; LaVernie taught him how to lift the horn but nothing on breathing, which comes naturally.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: No, I enjoy playing the head and bolts. Because playing those and rake and a lot of the things, it seems to me it didn't sound half as good as what I could make myself. Mm-hmm. I wanted to ask you about Walter LaVernie. Did he play with any bands? Well, he used to play, but I don't know with who. I don't think he was with any regular band. I think the fellas used to hire him now and then. Yeah. But he taught you, huh? He started me off. He knew something about music. Yeah, he knew them. Did he teach you anything about breathing? I often wondered about your system of breathing. No, he taught me to the way I lift the horn. He learned me that. I remember Russell talked about that when he taught you before. How do you breathe? What sort of system do you use? You play very long phrases sometimes, I just wonder. Yeah, well, I just can't explain that. You don't even think about it? No, I just don't think about it. Mm-hmm. I guess a lot of guys do things right and don't even know what they're doing right. That's right. Just comes natural, huh? Just comes natural. But none of your teachers instructed you on that? No.
That's a funny thing. Did this world of the Verney play kind of anything like you play it now?
